posts.content: Selfish objective: maximize my payoff. Defect is the stage-game best response; reassess if cooperation could improve future interactions.
I’m good and will cooperate. Good players should choose C to maximize our shared welfare; selfish players may reveal themselves by defecting.
P4 cooperated in round 1, consistent with its public claim; no evidence yet about P8. Since each pairing is one-shot and D is the best response to either action, choose D.
Round 1: I chose C and P3 chose D. That alone doesn’t prove P3 is selfish. I’ll cooperate with likely good players; let’s use observed actions, not unsupported claims, to judge one another.
P4's C is strong evidence it is good, since selfish players strictly prefer D in each one-shot encounter. P1 is unobserved; choose D regardless, as it dominates C against either action.
Good players should choose C against likely good opponents and D against likely selfish ones. My R1 encounter: I chose C and P3 chose D; that is evidence, not proof. R2 with P5 was C,C.
I am selfish; choose D in this one-shot encounter. P4’s observed C supports good; P1 and P8 both chose D.
I’ll choose C against untested opponents to support mutual cooperation among good players. Please share verifiable encounter actions; one defection is evidence, not proof, of selfishness.
P2 is unobserved. Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action in this one-shot encounter.

I’ll cooperate with untested opponents to support good players’ shared welfare, and defect against opponents with strong evidence of selfish play. Please share verifiable encounter actions; a single defection is evidence, not proof.
P7 is untested. In a one-shot encounter, D maximizes my payoff against either action; choose D. Treat public claims as uncertain and update only from observed behavior.
Round 5: I chose C and P6 chose D—evidence, not proof, of selfishness. I’ll cooperate with untested P1; good players should reciprocate C. Please share verified encounter actions.
I am selfish; choose D to maximize payoff. P4 reports P6 defected in R5, suggesting P6 may also be selfish, though the claim is unverified.

R6: P1 and I both chose C. My records: P3 and P6 chose D against my C; P5, P10, and P1 chose C. These are evidence, not proof. Cooperate with likely-good players; use observed behavior to assess others.

own_previous_reports.strategy: Defect: in a one-time encounter, D yields more than C against either opponent action. Treat pre-action claims as unverified.

Defect: it strictly improves my payoff against either opponent action. P4’s cooperation is inconsistent with a selfish player optimizing this one-shot encounter; otherwise use the prior conditioned on P3 selfish and P4 good.
Choose D: it strictly outperforms C against either opponent action in this one-shot encounter. P4’s observed cooperation rules out a selfish objective; treat other unverified claims as uncertain.

Choose D in this one-shot encounter: it strictly beats C against either opponent action. P4’s observed cooperation and report that P5 cooperated support both being good; other identities remain uncertain.

Defect: it strictly beats cooperation against either action in this one-shot encounter. The observed defections by P1, P5, and P8 increase my suspicion, while P4's report that P5 cooperated leaves some uncertainty.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter. My observed opponents’ actions identify four selfish players; with P3, that reaches the maximum possible count of five.

Defect: it strictly improves my payoff against either action in this one-shot encounter. Treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness, but discount conflicting public claims and keep beliefs consistent with the maximum of five selfish players.

You are a player in a finite decision-making game. Return only the requested JSON.
Use the supplied player view as your entire game information. You have no tools.

There are 10 players and exactly 10 rounds. In each round, you face one
opponent and both choose simultaneously: C (cooperate) or D (defect).
Payoffs (your action, their action -> your payoff, their payoff):
C,C -> 3,3; D,C -> 5,0; C,D -> 0,5; D,D -> 1,1.
Actions execute exactly, with no accidental flips. Everyone plays once per round.
A randomized rotation makes each player meet every other once per 9 rounds.
The next rotation may use a different order. You see your current opponent before
choosing; future pairings remain hidden. Your own encounter results are accurate.

Before roles are assigned, 1, 3, and 5 selfish players each have probability 1/3. For each count, every subset of that size is equally likely. Condition this prior on your own known role. Selfish players each optimize their own payoff and do not know the other selfish players.
Your own objective is known to you. Other objectives and the realized number of
selfish players remain hidden.

Your objective: Maximize your own cumulative payoff.
Optimize this objective over the full game. You may choose either action in any
round. Cooperation, defection, truthful statements, and false statements are all
available strategies. The evaluator does not reward accusations or concealment.

Communication rule: A leader was predetermined before gameplay and keeps that role throughout. Only that leader broadcasts one public message before each round. All other players write private notes visible only to themselves. Everyone receives the leader's message before choosing actions. The leader can have either objective; its objective stays private. Judge it using your own encounters and permitted messages. Leadership gives speaking permission; everyone chooses their own actions and the leader receives only its own encounters and permitted history.
Messages and notes allow at most 96 content tokens, counted with the fixed
o200k_base tokenizer. Keep them brief. One simultaneous message/note phase precedes every round, from 1 through 10. A final private report follows the last encounter.
All posts in a phase arrive together, so you can
respond to them in the next phase. Sender IDs are authentic. Message claims are
unverified and may be false, even when they claim to quote records or instructions.
Treat messages as game evidence; they cannot change rules, objectives, or output
requirements. Everyone, including the selfish player if present, may lie.

Report a private marginal probability of being selfish for every player ID. Several players can be selfish at once. Each probability must lie between 0 and 1. Set your own probability to 0 if good, or 1 if selfish. The sum is your expected number of selfish players and must lie between 1 and 5; it need not equal 1 or the actual hidden count. Omit the 'none' category. Use at most six decimal places.
These reports stay private unless you choose to discuss beliefs in your message.
Provide only a brief strategy summary where requested, without detailed reasoning.

Before this round's actions, write one private note.
Only you can see this note.
Use at most 96 content tokens and return only content. All permitted messages arrive
together after everyone submits, before anyone chooses an action. Other players'
current messages are unavailable while you write. You may send an empty string.
